questions.question: Which package manager is used by default on Amazon Linux?

options.text: apt
yum
pacman
brew

explanation.correct: YUM (Yellowdog Updater, Modified) is the default package manager on Amazon Linux and Red Hat-based distributions.
explanation.why: APT is used on Ubuntu/Debian. pacman is used on Arch Linux. brew is the macOS package manager.

questions.question: What is a Linux software repository?

options.text: A folder on your hard drive where you store downloaded files
A central storage location of verified packages for installation and updates
A backup of your operating system
A type of Linux file permission

explanation.correct: A repository is a central, trusted storage location from which Linux systems download and install software packages.
explanation.why: It is not a local folder, OS backup, or related to file permissions.

questions.question: What is the correct command to install Git on Amazon Linux without any confirmation prompts?

options.text: sudo apt install git
sudo yum get git -y
sudo yum install git -y
yum add git --yes

explanation.correct: sudo yum install git -y uses the yum package manager with the -y flag to automatically answer yes to all prompts.
explanation.why: apt is for Ubuntu/Debian. 'yum get' and 'yum add' are not valid commands.

questions.question: What does the -y flag do when used with a YUM command?

options.text: Installs the latest version only
Skips downloading and uses cache
Automatically answers yes to all prompts
Runs the command as root

explanation.correct: The -y flag tells YUM to automatically answer yes to all confirmation prompts, enabling non-interactive (scriptable) installations.
explanation.why: It does not control version selection, caching, or user privileges.

questions.question: Which command refreshes the repository metadata on Amazon Linux?

options.text: sudo yum upgrade -y
sudo yum update -y
sudo yum refresh -y
sudo yum sync -y

explanation.correct: sudo yum update -y refreshes (syncs) the local list of available packages from the remote repositories without installing anything.
explanation.why: upgrade installs newer versions of installed packages. 'refresh' and 'sync' are not standard YUM subcommands.

questions.question: What does 'sudo yum upgrade -y' do?

options.text: Refreshes repository metadata
Installs a new operating system
Updates all installed software to the latest versions available in the repository
Removes outdated packages

explanation.correct: yum upgrade downloads and installs newer versions of all currently installed packages based on what is available in the configured repositories.
explanation.why: Refreshing metadata is yum update. It does not install a new OS or automatically remove packages.

questions.question: In a 3-tier web application, which tier does Apache or Nginx belong to?

options.text: Backend tier
Database tier
Frontend tier
Load balancing tier

explanation.correct: Apache and Nginx are web server software that serve the frontend (client-facing) tier — they handle HTTP requests and deliver HTML/CSS/JS files to users' browsers.
explanation.why: Backend tier runs Node.js/Flask. Database tier runs MySQL. Load balancing is a separate networking concern.

questions.question: Where are repository configuration files stored on Amazon Linux?

options.text: /var/lib/rpm/
/etc/yum.repos.d/
/usr/share/repos/
/home/repos.d/

explanation.correct: On Amazon Linux (and all Red Hat-based distros), repository configuration files (.repo files) are located in /etc/yum.repos.d/.
explanation.why: /var/lib/rpm/ stores the RPM package database. The other paths do not exist as standard repo config locations.

questions.question: What package format does Amazon Linux use?

options.text: .deb
.pkg
.exe
.rpm

explanation.correct: Amazon Linux, like Red Hat and CentOS, uses the RPM (.rpm) package format.
explanation.why: .deb is used by Ubuntu/Debian. .pkg is used by macOS. .exe is a Windows executable, not a Linux package format.

questions.question: What does OS patching mean?

options.text: Reinstalling the operating system from scratch
Applying small code updates to fix or improve existing software without replacing it completely
Creating a backup of system files
Changing the file permissions on system directories

explanation.correct: Patching means applying targeted updates (fixes, security patches, performance improvements) to existing software without a full reinstallation.
explanation.why: Reinstalling the OS is a completely different operation. Patching is not backup creation or permission management.

questions.question: What is the correct order of operations when performing OS patching on a Linux server?

options.text: yum upgrade → yum update → reboot
yum install → yum update → yum upgrade
yum update → yum upgrade → verify
yum check-update → reboot → yum upgrade

explanation.correct: Always run yum update first to refresh repository metadata, then yum upgrade to install newer package versions, then verify the updates were applied.
explanation.why: Running upgrade before update means you're working with stale repository information. Rebooting before upgrading makes no sense.

questions.question: Which command shows detailed information about a software package including version, size, and repository source?

options.text: yum show git
yum details git
yum info git
yum describe git

explanation.correct: yum info <package> displays detailed package information including name, version, release, architecture, size, repository source, summary, and description.
explanation.why: 'yum show', 'yum details', and 'yum describe' are not valid YUM subcommands.

questions.question: A software package contains which of the following? (Choose the MOST complete answer)

options.text: Only the program executable files
Program files, dependencies, configuration files, and metadata
Program files and a README document
Dependencies and documentation only

explanation.correct: A complete Linux software package bundles program files (executables/libraries), dependency declarations, default configuration files, and metadata (version, license, description) — all compressed together.
explanation.why: Package contents go far beyond just executables. Options A, C, and D are incomplete descriptions.

questions.question: Why is it important to confirm with your team before running 'sudo yum upgrade -y' on a production server?

options.text: Because YUM requires administrator approval for each upgrade
Because upgrading can break existing applications that depend on specific software versions
Because yum upgrade deletes your configuration files
Because yum upgrade shuts down all running services

explanation.correct: Upgrading packages can introduce version incompatibilities that break existing applications. For example, upgrading Python from 3.8 to 3.11 could break apps written for 3.8.
explanation.why: YUM does not require team approval by design. Upgrade does not delete config files or shut down services automatically.

questions.question: How does Linux handle software updates differently from Windows?

options.text: Linux automatically installs updates in the background without any action from the admin
Linux shows pop-up notifications that force immediate restarts
Linux requires admins to manually check for and apply updates — no pop-up notifications
Linux updates are more expensive than Windows updates

explanation.correct: Linux servers have no GUI pop-up notification system for updates. Admins must proactively run yum check-update or set up automation scripts to monitor and apply patches.
explanation.why: Linux does not auto-install patches silently, force restarts, or involve any cost for updates.

questions.question: Which command checks if a specific package (git) has any available updates without installing them?

options.text: sudo yum update git
sudo yum check-update git
sudo yum verify git
yum info git --updates

explanation.correct: sudo yum check-update git checks if a newer version of git is available in the configured repositories without downloading or installing anything.
explanation.why: yum update git would actually download and install the update. The other options are not valid YUM commands.

questions.question: In the 3-tier architecture, what is the role of the backend (Tier 2)?

options.text: To serve HTML files to the user's browser
To store user data persistently
To process requests, apply business logic, and interact with the database
To manage network routing between tiers

explanation.correct: The backend tier (Node.js, Flask, etc.) receives requests from the frontend, processes them using business logic, validates data, and interacts with the database to retrieve or store information.
explanation.why: Serving HTML is the frontend's job. Storing data is the database's job. Network routing is infrastructure, not a tier.

questions.question: Who is responsible for maintaining the official Amazon Linux repositories?

options.text: The open-source community only
Amazon itself, along with some third-party maintainers
Canonical Limited
Red Hat

explanation.correct: Amazon maintains the official Amazon Linux repositories, ensuring packages are tested, verified, and kept up to date. Some third-party software (like Google or Docker packages) is maintained by those respective organizations.
explanation.why: Canonical Limited maintains Ubuntu repositories. Red Hat maintains RHEL repositories. The open-source community contributes but official repos are controlled by the distributor.

questions.question: After installing a package with YUM, where are the executable files typically placed?

options.text: /home/packages/
/var/lib/rpm/
/usr/bin/ or /bin/
/etc/installed/

explanation.correct: Executables (command files) are placed in /usr/bin/, /usr/local/bin/, or /bin/ after RPM package installation, following Linux filesystem hierarchy standards.
explanation.why: /home/packages/ is not a standard location. /var/lib/rpm/ stores the RPM database metadata. /etc/ stores configuration files, not executables.

questions.question: A Linux administrator notices the server is running Git 2.39. A critical security vulnerability was announced in Git 2.39. What is the correct patching workflow?

options.text: Uninstall Git, then reinstall the latest version
Run sudo yum upgrade -y immediately to fix all packages
Check current version → check for update → review with team → apply patch with sudo yum update git -y → verify version
Download the new Git source code and compile it manually

explanation.correct: The correct workflow: verify current version, check if a patched version is available (yum check-update git), confirm with the team, apply the specific package update, and verify the new version is installed.
explanation.why: Uninstalling/reinstalling is not patching. Upgrading all packages blindly is risky. Compiling from source is unnecessary when package managers handle this.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'yum update' (without specifying a package)?

options.text: It installs all available software from the repository
It refreshes the list of packages and their versions from the remote repositories
It removes outdated packages from the system
It reinstalls all currently installed packages

explanation.correct: yum update (also written as yum makecache) synchronizes the local package metadata with the remote repository, telling the system which software versions are currently available — no actual installation happens.
explanation.why: Installing all software, removing outdated packages, and reinstalling packages are all different operations.

questions.question: You want to install Nginx, Python3, and MySQL in one command. Which is correct?

options.text: sudo yum install nginx && sudo yum install python3 && sudo yum install mysql
sudo yum install nginx python3 mysql -y
sudo yum install [nginx, python3, mysql] -y
sudo yum batch-install nginx python3 mysql

explanation.correct: YUM accepts multiple package names separated by spaces in a single install command. This installs all three packages in one transaction, resolving shared dependencies efficiently.
explanation.why: Chaining with && works but is less efficient. Square bracket syntax and 'batch-install' are not valid YUM formats.

questions.question: What happens internally when you run 'sudo yum install apache' on Amazon Linux?

options.text: YUM downloads Apache from apache.org and installs it
YUM searches the configured repositories, resolves dependencies, downloads all required packages, and installs them
YUM copies Apache from another server on the same network
YUM checks Windows Update servers for the package

explanation.correct: YUM queries the configured repository metadata, identifies the package and all dependencies, downloads them from the repository URL, verifies GPG signatures, and installs everything in the correct order.
explanation.why: YUM does not download directly from the vendor's website — it always uses configured repositories. It does not copy from network servers or contact Windows servers.

questions.question: A company runs a web application with Apache on Python 2.7. They want to run 'sudo yum upgrade -y' to apply security patches. What is the PRIMARY risk?

options.text: The server will run out of disk space
Apache may be upgraded to a version that drops Python 2.7 support, breaking the application
YUM will delete the application's source code
The upgrade will change file permissions on /var/www/html/

explanation.correct: Running a blanket upgrade can update Python, Apache, or shared libraries to versions that are incompatible with the existing application code. Python 2.7 is end-of-life and packages depending on it may break when underlying libraries are upgraded.
explanation.why: YUM upgrade doesn't cause disk space issues, delete application code, or change web directory permissions.

questions.question: Which AWS service can automate OS patching across many EC2 instances without manual SSH access?

options.text: AWS CloudWatch
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
AWS Config
AWS Trusted Advisor

explanation.correct: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates the process of patching managed EC2 instances, allowing you to define patch baselines, schedule maintenance windows, and verify compliance across your fleet — all without logging into individual instances.
explanation.why: CloudWatch monitors metrics. AWS Config tracks resource configurations. Trusted Advisor gives optimization recommendations. None of these automate patching.

questions.question: When a user opens facebook.com and the login page appears, which tier is primarily responsible for delivering that page?

options.text: Tier 2 — Backend (Node.js/Flask)
Tier 3 — Database (MySQL)
Tier 1 — Frontend Web Server (Apache/Nginx)
A load balancer, not any tier

explanation.correct: The web server (Apache/Nginx) in Tier 1 receives the HTTP request and serves the login page HTML/CSS/JS files to the user's browser. This is a static file delivery operation — the backend is not involved until the user submits the form.
explanation.why: The backend processes form submissions, not page delivery. The database stores data and is not involved in serving UI files. Load balancers route traffic but don't serve content.

questions.question: A DevOps engineer writes an automation script that runs 'sudo yum update -y && sudo yum upgrade -y' every Sunday at 2 AM. What is the biggest concern with this approach in a production environment?

options.text: YUM commands can only be run during business hours
Automatic package upgrades could break applications due to unexpected version changes
The -y flag does not work in cron jobs
sudo does not work in automated scripts

explanation.correct: Automatically upgrading all packages without review can introduce breaking changes. A new minor version of a shared library could cause application failures. Production automation should use yum update (security patches only) or carefully curated patch baselines, not blanket upgrades.
explanation.why: YUM has no time restrictions. -y works in cron jobs. sudo works in scripts with proper configuration.

questions.question: What is the difference between application software and utility software in Linux?

options.text: Application software requires root privileges; utility software does not
Application software provides end-user/service functionality (Apache, MySQL); utility software provides supporting tools (vim, chmod, ls)
Application software is installed via YUM; utility software is built into the kernel
There is no meaningful difference — both are the same category

explanation.correct: Application software delivers specific functionality to end users or services (web server, database, runtime). Utility software provides helper tools for system administration tasks (text editors, permission tools, file management commands).
explanation.why: Privilege requirements vary for both categories. Both can be installed via YUM. They are meaningfully different categories.

questions.question: A company in Mumbai has an EC2 instance running Amazon Linux 2023. After running 'sudo yum check-update git', the output shows: 'Warning: New release of Amazon Linux is available.' What does this mean?

options.text: Git has a critical security update that must be applied immediately
The current Amazon Linux 2023 instance is outdated and must be upgraded
The system is on the current version of Amazon Linux 2023, but a newer major Amazon Linux release exists
The YUM repository connection has failed

explanation.correct: This warning simply means there is a newer major version of Amazon Linux available (e.g., moving from AL2023 to a future release). It does not mean your current OS or Git is insecure — it is an informational notice about an available major OS upgrade, not a patch requirement.
explanation.why: This is not a Git vulnerability notice. The OS is not 'outdated' in the security sense. Repository connections still work fine when this warning appears.

questions.question: A developer tells you: 'We need to add third-party software X to our servers. The vendor provides an official YUM repository.' What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Download the .rpm file manually from the vendor website and install with rpm -ivh
Add the vendor's official .repo file to /etc/yum.repos.d/ and then install via yum
Compile the software from source code for maximum security
Install it on one server manually and clone the disk image to other servers

explanation.correct: The recommended approach is to add the vendor's official repository configuration to /etc/yum.repos.d/ — this integrates the third-party repo with YUM, enabling automated dependency resolution, GPG signature verification, and future updates via yum upgrade.
explanation.why: Manual RPM installs lose automatic dependency resolution and future update tracking. Compiling from source is complex and not necessary when official repos exist. Disk cloning is not a scalable or maintainable software management approach.
